knowledge_point.title: Calculating a Scalar Projection Using Angles and Magnitudes

question.:question/problem: Suppose $|\,c\,|=18$ and the angle between vectors $c$ and $d$ is $\theta =\frac{3\pi }{4}.$ Find the scalar projection of $c$ onto $d.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{d}\,c & =|\,c\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =18\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4}) \\  & =18\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =-9\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

generation.origin: observed homogeneous bank evidence

question.:question/problem: Suppose $|\,a\,|=3$ and the angle between vectors $a$ and $b$ is $\theta =\frac{5\pi }{6}.$ Find the scalar projection of $a$ onto $b.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =|\,a\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{6}) \\  & =3\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
